subject: Elmbridge post-incident reconstruction, owners, and exec-readiness checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <s.lowe@elmbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Elmbridge SRE <sre@elmbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Search latency & 5xx spike affecting Elmbridge production

Marcus —

Following our monitoring and customer reports, Elmbridge saw a sustained latency spike (p95 from ~220ms to ~1.8s) and an increase in 5xx responses starting Nov 5 18:40 PST and recurring through early hours Nov 6. Impact: search queries for logged-in users degraded, several customers reported timeouts during checkout flows.

We need:
- A concise RCA (technical + timeline) we can share with our execs tomorrow morning.
- A list of corrective actions, owners, and ETA for code fixes and configuration changes.
- Confirmation on whether you will provide any billing credits / SLA remediation.

I've attached a short incident summary from our side (elmbridge-incident-summary.pdf). We are available for a technical bridge if helpful. Please advise next steps and a guaranteed readout time for our executives.

Thanks,
Samantha Lowe
Head of Prod Ops | Elmbridge Systems

Attachment: elmbridge-incident-summary.pdf (pdf, 232 KB)

Samantha, can you confirm if 11:30 PST works for a short bridge? We will also prepare a readout slide deck for your execs and share it prior to the call.

—Marcus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lowe <s.lowe@elmbridge.com>, Elmbridge SRE <sre@elmbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 07:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Elmbridge — RCA draft (v1) and mitigation timeline

Team / Samantha —

Quick summary (RCA v1):
- Symptom: p95 latency spike and elevated 5xx between 2027-11-05T18:40:00Z and 2027-11-06T04:10:00Z.
- Root cause (probable): Regression introduced in our recent autoscaling routing change (rollout 2027-11-05 17:55 PST) caused uneven distribution of long-sequence chat requests to a small subset of pods that had an incompatible kernel fallback path; that fallback path triggered repeated full KV-cache invalidations under load causing increased token decode time and backend 503s when queue depth exceeded thresholds.
- Evidence: kernel fallback logs (INF runtime) show repeated fallback from avx512 to scalar path on 3 host IDs (host-07a, host-0b3, host-11f) coincident with error bursts; prometheus graphs attached to the internal ticket; heap snapshots and GC spikes correlated.

Immediate mitigations applied (11:15–12:40 PST):
- Rolled back autoscaler routing change (rollout rollback completed at 11:28 PST).
- Temporarily pinned Elmbridge traffic to the previously stable model variant and forced KV-cache warming on affected pools.
- Added a short-lived rate limit on long-sequence user requests to reduce burst load.

Planned remediation (owners & ETA):
- Neha: deploy patched kernel selection logic (PR #4721) to staging by 2027-11-08 10:00 PST, canary to production 2027-11-09 02:00 PST, full rollout 2027-11-09 08:00 PST.
- Kimberly: coordinate SLA impact calc and proposal for credits by 2027-11-08 EOD.
- Marcus: lead exec readout and finalize slides; confirm schedule with Elmbridge.
- Ops Follow-up: 7-day elevated monitoring window with daily status to Elmbridge (owner: Neha).

Attachments: elmbridge_rca_v1.pdf (draft, includes logs snippet and timeline)

Notes: This draft still needs the exact token accounting to quantify customer impact (drop-in error counts by route). I’ll add the numeric table after we reconcile the access logs.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Site Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
